fields.label: Inventory Item GID
fields.description: Cached deliberately. Without it every inventory push costs an extra API call to look it up, which is what makes the existing ecommerce_integrations app spend two calls per item.

fields.label: Online Store Publish Done
fields.description: Set once the app has made its one and only decision about putting this product on the Online Store. Whether it ends up published after that is the merchant's to change; the app never revisits it, and never reads Shopify about it again.

fields.label: App Media
fields.description: Which Shopify media this app created, as {file_url: media id}. It is the only thing that distinguishes an image the app uploaded from photography the merchant added in the Shopify admin, which is never moved or deleted.

fields.label: Initial State Pushed
fields.description: Set the moment this link's opening stock, price and images are queued -- not when those rows drain. The watermarks below are written on drain, which leaves a window where every inbound products/update re-queues the same three pushes; on 3 October that window produced 70 inventory, 69 price and 103 media rows for a single item.

fields.label: Inbound Digest
fields.description: A hash of the Shopify fields this app maps onto the Item, as of the last webhook that changed anything. A products/update whose digest matches is Shopify echoing our own mutation back, and is dropped without saving the Item.

fields.label: Is Template
fields.description: This row is the variant template's own record of which Shopify product it owns, not a sellable variant: it carries a product_gid and no variant_gid. Before it existed a template's product could only be inferred backwards from its children's rows, so an echo that corrupted one child's template_item detached the whole range -- and disabling a single size then created a second Shopify product for it.
